To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
New Zealand nurses have a low to average level of burnout.
the nurses we surveyed are doing well, with only a small minority experiencing burnout.

1) the level of burnout in our sample of nurses was low to average, 2) the level of emotional exhaustion in our sample of registered nurses was low, 3) the level of depersonalisation in our sample of enrolled nurses was low, and 4) the level of personal accomplishment in our sample of graduate nurses was average.
In summary, our research is concerned with
burnout and its implications for nursing.
the identification of the extent and severity levels of burnout and the development of a model for the prevention of burnout in the nursing profession.
the development and validation of a New Zealand version of the Maslach Inventory of Burnout.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the New Zealand nursing population is experiencing a level of burnout that is not dissimilar from that reported in other countries, although the results do indicate that the New Zealand population may be less susceptible to burnout than those of other nations.
burnout in New Zealand nurses is a problem but not an epidemic.
the New Zealand nursing profession has been spared the 'cancer' of burnout, at least for the moment, and the reasons for this are not yet clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
burnout, in its early stages, can be prevented or minimised through the use of effective strategies and techniques.
the nurses who participated in this study were doing reasonably well in terms of avoiding or not progressing to the more advanced stages of burnout.
New Zealand nurses are not as badly off as their overseas counterparts and that there are a number of reasons to be positive about the future of nursing in New Zealand.
The main takeaway from our work is that
burnout is an issue that should not be ignored by nurses and nursing managers.
burnout in nurses is a significant problem and needs to be addressed.

the MBI is an effective instrument for measuring burnout and the Phase Model is a useful tool for identifying nurses who are at risk of progressing to the advanced stages of burnout and for developing appropriate intervention strategies to prevent this from happening.
